sections.html:
Cecil County is the northeastern corner of Maryland, touching Pennsylvania and Delaware. Elkton is both the seat of government and the biggest town. The 2020 census counted 103,725 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 107,131.

Elkton had 6,386 housing units in 2020, with 6.9% of them vacant. That is a thin supply of empty homes, so a tidy house priced sensibly is not up against piles of empty stock. About 72 of the county's 418 square miles are water, so owners near the bay and the Elk River should expect flood and drainage questions from buyers and lenders.

The county rate is $0.9724 per $100 of assessed value, down from $0.9824. The state adds $0.112, so a house outside any town pays $1.0844 per $100. Municipalities layer a separate levy over that, which is why neighbors a few miles apart can see very different totals.

Elkton carries the highest combined rate among the towns. A buyer comparing an Elkton house with a same-priced house in the open county will see a noticeably bigger bill, and you should be ready for that conversation.

Residential full cash value in Cecil County rose 15.1% between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026. Statewide, the comparable group rose 13.2%. Notices went out December 30, 2025. Any jump is spread in equal steps across three tax years, so the taxable figure on your bill can lag behind current market value.

The county's assessable base is about $14.6 billion for fiscal 2026, with $15.4 billion projected for fiscal 2027.

Homestead credit

If you live in the home, you apply once for the homestead credit. It limits how much taxable value can climb in a year. The cap for unincorporated Cecil County is 4% for July 1, 2026. Counties and towns can change their caps until March 15, so check the current number with the assessment office. The buyer does not inherit your capped value, since the cap resets after a sale. Mention that when a buyer asks what the bill will be.

Notices arrive in July. A full-year bill is interest-free through September and goes delinquent October 1. If the house is your principal residence, you can split it: the first half by September 30, the rest by December 31. Semi-annual billing is also open to some commercial property.

Past-due balances gain 1% interest each month, and a 3% late fee lands on March 1.

  • Pay at the Finance Office, 200 Chesapeake Blvd., Suite 1100, Elkton, or online.
  • E-check and card payments carry a third-party convenience fee.
  • From May 1, taxes must be paid with cash, a cashier's or certified check, a money order or certain credit cards.
  • A returned check costs $35.
  • A lender that escrows your tax can pull the bill electronically, but send your own copy as well.

Rate questions go to tax@ccgov.org. The state assessment office answers at 410-996-2760.

sections.h2: How the Cecil County tax sale works
sections.html:
The county sells unpaid tax online each June through RealAuction. In 2025, pre-registration ran May 16 to 23, bidding opened May 31, and the sale closed in early June. Closing times have varied, so call the Finance Office before you count on any date.

  1. Delinquency notices go out March 1.
  2. A local newspaper runs the advertisement four weeks in a row.
  3. Bidders pre-register and pay a $100 non-refundable deposit.
  4. If a winning bid runs above 40% of the property's full cash value, the buyer pays a 20% premium on the excess. That premium comes back if the certificate is redeemed or foreclosed within two years.

You keep the right to redeem until a court cuts it off. A buyer may start a foreclosure case six months and one day after the sale. The county does not handle foreclosure itself.

sections.h2: Credits and deferrals that matter when you sell
sections.html:
The county offers a Senior Tax Credit and a second credit for former service members, each worth 20% off the county tax. Thresholds include household income under $92,000 and a dwelling assessed at $375,000 or less, with a September 1 deadline. State credits, exemptions and a deferral program are also available.

The elderly and disabled deferral is the one that changes a closing. It postpones only the year-over-year increase in county tax. What was postponed gets recorded as a lien, and it comes due when you sell or move.

  • Eligibility starts at age 65 with five years in the home and household income of $60,000 or less.
  • The lien turns up in the title search, and the title company folds it into your payoff.
  • Other exemptions include $15,000 off the assessment for blind owners and a full exemption for disabled service members with a 100% permanent service-connected disability.

Amounts and limits shift, so verify them with the Finance Office before quoting a buyer any figure. While you still live there, ask whether any credit you hold ends at the sale, and whether the county will prorate the bill between you and the buyer on the settlement statement. Proration is normally handled by the title company, but the numbers it uses come from the Finance Office records, so an old address or a missing credit on file can throw the figures off.

Call the Finance Office first, then go down this list.

  1. Ask what is owed and whether the account has been sent to the June sale.
  2. Check for a deferral lien left from a past credit program.
  3. Find out whether a town bill also applies, for example in Elkton or North East.
  4. Request a payoff that holds through the closing date, because interest keeps adding 1% a month.

On closing day the title company sends the county and any town their money out of your proceeds, and the settlement statement shows each line. If the house also needs repairs, a cash sale as-is puts the tax payoff on that statement and stops the monthly penalties without a round of fix-ups, inspections and repair credits.

Bring the latest bill, any deferral paperwork and your homestead approval to the first call. It saves a second trip. Where both a town bill and a county bill exist, ask for a payoff on each, because the town and the county are paid as different accounts and each has its own interest clock. Once both are paid, ask for written confirmation and file it with your closing papers.

faqs.q: How much is the Cecil County tax rate?
faqs.a: Cecil charges $0.9724 per $100 of assessed value and the state adds $0.112, which totals $1.0844 per $100 outside a town.

faqs.q: Which Cecil County town has the highest property tax?
faqs.a: Elkton, at a combined $1.7200 per $100. Cecilton is lowest among the listed towns at $1.4109.

faqs.q: What happens if I pay late?
faqs.a: Past-due balances gain 1% interest each month, and a 3% late fee lands on March 1.

faqs.q: When is the Cecil County tax sale?
faqs.a: Online, every June. The 2025 sale opened for bids May 31 and wrapped up in early June.

faqs.q: Must a tax deferral be repaid when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. A deferred amount is recorded as a lien and has to be repaid when the owner sells or moves out.
